rules.title: Arizona — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Employer may require 90 days of employment before use (hires after 2017-07-01). Leave is used in the smaller of hourly increments or the smallest payroll increment; use may be capped at 40 hours a year (24 hours for employers under 15).

rules.title: Arizona (15+ employees) — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Unused leave carries over (carryover may be capped at 40 hours for employers with 15+); instead of carryover the employer may pay out unused leave at year end and frontload the next year. No payout at separation; balances reinstated on rehire within 9 months.

rules.title: Arizona (<15 employees) — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Unused leave carries over (carryover may be capped at 24 hours for employers under 15); instead of carryover the employer may pay out unused leave at year end and frontload the next year. No payout at separation; balances reinstated on rehire within 9 months.

rules.title: California — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin on the 90th day of employment; the employer may set a minimum increment of up to 2 hours and may cap use at 40 hours or 5 days a year (SB 616, 2024).

rules.title: California — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Accrued leave carries over; the total balance may be capped at 80 hours or 10 days. Frontloading 40 hours/5 days at the start of each year removes the carryover duty. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within one year.

rules.title: Colorado — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Leave may be used as it accrues (no waiting period); taken in hourly increments or smaller as the employer permits; use may be capped at 48 hours a year.

rules.title: Colorado — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 48 hours of unused leave carries forward; frontloading 48 hours satisfies the duty. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 6 months.

rules.title: Connecticut — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin on the 120th calendar day of employment (was 680 hours before 2025); employer may require one-hour increments; use may be capped at 40 hours a year. Covers employers with 25+ employees in 2025, 11+ from 2026-01-01 and 1+ from 2027-01-01.

rules.title: Connecticut — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours of unused leave carries over; alternatively the employer may make 40 hours available at the start of the year. No payout at separation unless policy provides.

rules.title: District of Columbia — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin after 90 days of service; leave is taken in the smallest payroll increment, no larger than one hour; annual use is limited to the accrual cap (3, 5 or 7 days by employer size).

rules.title: District of Columbia — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Unused leave carries over with no cap on the balance, though use stays capped at the annual accrual amount. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within one year.

rules.title: Illinois — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Paid Leave for All Workers: use may begin 90 days after employment starts (or 2024-03-31 for existing staff); minimum increment up to 2 hours (or the scheduled workday if shorter); use may be capped at 40 hours a year.

citations.source: IDOL Paid Leave for All Workers

rules.title: Illinois — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Accrued unused leave carries over (carryover may be capped at 40 hours); frontloading 40 hours removes the carryover duty. No payout at separation unless the leave sits in a PTO bank.

citations.source: IDOL Paid Leave for All Workers

rules.title: Massachusetts — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin on the 90th day of employment; leave is taken in the smaller of hourly increments or the smallest payroll increment; use may be capped at 40 hours a year.

rules.title: Massachusetts — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours of unused earned sick time carries over; lump-sum frontloading of 40 hours removes the carryover duty. No payout at separation.

rules.title: Maryland — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Employer may deny use during the first 106 calendar days of employment; minimum increment may be set up to 4 hours; use may be capped at 64 hours a year.

rules.title: Maryland — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours carries over and the balance may be capped at 64 hours; frontloading the full annual amount removes the carryover duty. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 37 weeks.

rules.title: Maine — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Earned Paid Leave: employer may restrict use for the first 120 days of employment; increments of up to one hour; use may be capped at 40 hours a year.

rules.title: Maine — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours of unused leave carries over (frontloading 40 hours satisfies the duty, per DOL rules). No payout at separation unless policy provides; balance reinstated on rehire within one year.

rules.title: Michigan — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Earned Sick Time Act (as amended 2025-02-21): employer may require 120 days of employment before use for new hires; leave used in one-hour increments or the smaller payroll increment; use may be capped at 72 hours a year (40 for small businesses with 10 or fewer employees).

rules.title: Michigan (11+ employees) — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 72 hours of unused leave carries over; a frontloading employer need not allow carryover. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 2 months.

rules.title: Michigan (small business, 10 or fewer) — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Small businesses (10 or fewer employees): up to 40 hours of unused leave carries over; frontloading removes the duty. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 2 months.

rules.title: Minnesota — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Earned Sick and Safe Time is usable as it accrues; increments follow the payroll system (at least 15 minutes, never forced in blocks over 4 hours); accrual may be capped at 48 hours a year.

rules.title: Minnesota — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Unused ESST carries over up to an 80-hour balance. Alternatives: frontload 48 hours and pay out the unused balance at year end, or frontload 80 hours with no payout. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 180 days.

rules.title: New Jersey — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin on the 120th calendar day of employment; the employer sets the increment, up to the length of the scheduled shift; use may be capped at 40 hours a benefit year.

rules.title: New Jersey — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours carries over. An employer that frontloads must still either pay out unused time in the final month of the benefit year or carry it forward; an accruing employer may offer a payout the employee can accept. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 6 months.

rules.title: New Mexico — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Healthy Workplaces Act leave is usable as it accrues; taken in the smaller of hourly increments or the smallest payroll increment; use may be capped at 64 hours a year.

rules.title: New Mexico — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Accrued unused leave carries over with no cap on the balance; annual use stays capped at 64 hours; frontloading 64 hours is allowed but does not remove carryover. No payout at separation.

rules.title: Nevada — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Paid leave (SB 312) may be used from the 90th calendar day of employment; employer may set a minimum increment of up to 4 hours; use may be capped at 40 hours a year.

rules.title: Nevada — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours of unused paid leave carries over; frontloading the full amount on day one avoids carryover. No payout at separation required.

rules.title: New York — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Sick leave is usable as it accrues (from 2021-01-01); employer may set a minimum increment of up to 4 hours; use may be capped at 40 hours (fewer than 100 employees) or 56 hours (100+).

rules.title: New York — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Unused sick leave carries over with no cap on the balance, though annual use may be capped at 40 or 56 hours; frontloading does not remove carryover. No payout at separation.

rules.title: Oregon — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Sick time may be used starting the 91st calendar day of employment; taken in hourly increments (or smaller); use may be capped at 40 hours a year.

rules.title: Oregon — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours carries over and the balance may be capped at 80 hours; frontloading 40 hours at the start of the year removes the carryover duty. No payout at separation.

rules.title: Rhode Island — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin on the 90th calendar day of employment (150 days for seasonal, 180 for temporary employees); employer may set an increment of up to 4 hours; use may be capped at 40 hours a year (from 2020).

rules.title: Rhode Island — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours carries over; the employer may instead pay out unused time at year end and frontload the next year. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 135 days.

rules.title: Vermont — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Employer may impose a waiting period of up to one year before accrued time is used (accrual starts on day one); increments follow the payroll system; use may be capped at 40 hours a year.

rules.title: Vermont — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours of unused earned sick time carries over; frontloading the full annual amount removes the duty. No payout at separation unless policy provides.

rules.title: Washington — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin on the 90th calendar day of employment; leave is taken in the increments the payroll system uses, no larger than one hour; there is no cap on annual use.

rules.title: Washington — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours of unused paid sick leave carries over each year; frontloading does not remove the duty for hours left unused. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 12 months.

rules.title: Alaska Paid Sick Leave — 15+ employees (1 hr per 30 hrs, up to 56 hrs/yr)

result.summary: Ballot Measure 1 (2024), effective 2025-07-01: 1 hour of paid sick leave per 30 hours worked; accrual and use may be capped at 56 hours a year for employers with 15 or more employees.

rules.title: Alaska Paid Sick Leave — <15 employees (1 hr per 30 hrs, up to 40 hrs/yr)

result.summary: Ballot Measure 1 (2024), effective 2025-07-01: 1 hour of paid sick leave per 30 hours worked; accrual and use may be capped at 40 hours a year for employers with fewer than 15 employees.

rules.title: Alaska — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Leave is usable as it accrues (no waiting period in the measure); DOL guidance allows hourly increments or the smallest increment the employer tracks; annual use is limited to the 40/56-hour accrual cap.

rules.title: Alaska — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Unused balances carry over with no cap on the balance (use stays capped at 40/56 hours a year). No payout at separation; a voluntary cash-out may be offered. Balance reinstated on rehire within 6 months.

rules.title: Nebraska Paid Sick Time — 20+ employees (1 hr per 30 hrs, up to 56 hrs/yr)

result.summary: Healthy Families and Workplaces Act (Initiative 436, as amended by LB 415), effective 2025-10-01: 1 hour per 30 hours worked, up to 56 hours a year for employers with 20 or more employees. Employees under 16 and those working under 80 hours a year in Nebraska are excluded.

citations.source: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§48-3601 to 48-3611 (Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, Initiative 436; LB 415 2025)

rules.title: Nebraska Paid Sick Time — 11-19 employees (1 hr per 30 hrs, up to 40 hrs/yr)

result.summary: Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, effective 2025-10-01: 1 hour per 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours a year for employers with 11 to 19 employees; employers with 10 or fewer are exempt (LB 415).

citations.source: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§48-3601 to 48-3611 (Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, Initiative 436; LB 415 2025)
Nebraska DOL Paid Sick Time FAQ

rules.title: Nebraska — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Accrual and use begin after 80 hours of consecutive employment in Nebraska (LB 415); leave is taken in the smaller of hourly increments or the payroll system's smallest increment; annual use is limited to the 40/56-hour cap.

citations.source: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§48-3601 to 48-3611 (Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, Initiative 436; LB 415 2025)
Nebraska DOL Paid Sick Time FAQ

rules.title: Nebraska — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Unused sick time carries over with no cap on the balance; the employer may instead pay out unused time if the employee starts the new year with the full annual amount. No payout at separation; unpaid balances reinstated on rehire within 12 months.

citations.source: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§48-3601 to 48-3611 (Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, Initiative 436; LB 415 2025)
